Name: Ain Ghazal / Ibn el-Ghazzi (עין ע'זאל / אבן אל-ע'אזי)
Description: A complex water system including artificial channels (two long, two short) leading to 'wells' (interpreted as reservoirs/basins) in a shallow depression. This system was designed to collect and store runoff water from a catchment area of about 29 dunams, potentially holding up to 13,900 cubic meters. A settlement located on the eastern outskirts of Amman, Jordan, near a spring.

Name: Atlit-Yam (עתלית ים)
Description: A well, approximately 6 meters deep, demonstrating advanced hydrological and engineering knowledge, construction capabilities, and quarrying skills of the inhabitants. Another well at the site was only partially excavated.

Name: Beidha (ביידא)
Description: A settlement where travertine deposits near Bir Abu Rujha and along a sandstone cliff indicate the presence of a now-dry spring that supplied water. The site's location in a valley allowed for rainwater collection and channeling to create moist soil conditions, and water cisterns might also have been used.

Name: Beisamoun (בייסמון)
Description: A settlement established in clear proximity to the stable and abundant Einan springs, which remain significant water sources today.

Name: Gilgal I (גלגל 1)
Description: A prehistoric settlement where travertine deposits up to 3 meters thick indicate the presence of an ancient spring, now dry, which served as the water source for the community.

Name: Jericho (יריחו)
Description: A settlement from the Pre-Pottery Neolithic A period, located near the Elisha Spring in the Jordan Valley.

Name: Khirbet Jarassur (ח'רבת ג'אראסור)
Description: A well, briefly reported from Northern Iraq, without detailed information, dimensions, or drawings. It was considered the oldest well in the world by some researchers before the discovery at Atlit-Yam.

Name: Netiv HaGdud (נתיב הגדוד)
Description: A settlement established near a freshwater lake (Lake Salibiya), which formed as the Lisan Lake receded, indicating a wetter climate than today.

Name: Yiftah'el (יפתחאל)
Description: A settlement located near the Ein Yiftah'el spring in the Lower Galilee.
